newsitem.title: PERU: Peru peace broker raps media for causing confusion.
newsitem.headline: Peru peace broker raps media for causing confusion.

text.p: A mediator chided the news media for causing confusion in Peru's 15-week hostage crisis late on Wednesday as talks remained deadlocked over guerrilla demands for the release of jailed comrades.
Archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani upbraided news media for misreporting the siege at the Japanese ambassador's home, where Marxist rebels have held 72 VIPs since mid-December.
"There is superficial journalism which perhaps is not well-informed, or which perhaps is receiving information designed to create confusion," he told reporters.
"It would be good for certain news media to exercise a bit more respect," said Cipriani, the Vatican's representative on a three-man mediation team known as the guarantors commission.

Both President Alberto Fujimori and the Japanese embassy took great pains on Wednesday to deny a newspaper story that said Fujimori would fly to Tokyo to work out a solution to the standoff with Japanese officials.

Cipriani also objected to local news stories suggesting he was seeking the release of jailed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) members to speed up a peaceful settlement to the siege that began Dec. 17 when gunmen stormed a reception at the ambassador's residence and took the guests hostage.

Three months of talks have failed to reach any agreement and both mediators and hostages are showing signs of fatigue and frustration. Cipriani said this week that Peru's "heart is completely broken" by the siege.

Cipriani, Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent and Red Cross representative Michel Minning met for several hours with the guerrillas on Wednesday inside the residence. But there is no date for a resumption of direct talks with the government.

Fujimori, who has rejected the MRTA's demand for the freeing of about 400 jailed comrades, announced on Wednesday he will travel to Bolivia this weekend to discuss the crisis with Bolivian President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada.
Bolivian ambassador Jorge Gumucio is among the hostages being held by MRTA, whose demands include the release of four MRTA militants held in Bolivian jails.
The hostages include Fujimori's brother, two ministers, military officers and Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
In a bizarre development, a Norwegian tourist flew near the besieged house in a paraglider on Wednesday. Police ordered the unidentified man to land and arrested him.
"It seems he flew towards the residence by accident. He has not been charged with anything," a police spokesman said.

Police stationed around the diplomatic residence have got tougher with curious on-lookers. Three Austrian tourists were briefly detained on Wednesday for taking pictures and a U.S. tourist was arrested nearby this week.
The gloom surrounding the standoff was interrupted on Wednesday evening by birthday greetings for one of the hostages, national police Col. Francisco Salinas.

"Happy birthday dad," a young girl shouted through a megaphone from the street, while family and friends sang happy birthday. A man, presumably Salinas, appeared at a window, and applause could be heard inside the house after the singing.
